reason: The support cells' curled membrane sheets suggest they can insulate the motor neuron fibers, matching the current goal.
expectation: The support cells will wrap the fibers to form insulated outgoing nerve routes.

effect: The support cells wrapped the motor fibers, creating motor nerves and revealing the goal of connecting sight to muscle commands.
reaction: The segmented wrapping makes the support cells' role clearer.
reason: The eyes need a route to carry visual information toward the central nervous system, and the sensory nerves point toward a central connection.
expectation: The sensory nerves will connect to the eyes to carry visual signals toward the central nervous system.

effect: The eyes and sensory nerves formed a visual information route, which still needs to connect to muscle commands.
reaction: The change from light rays to a nerve signal makes the route clearer.
reason: The central nervous system is the likely connection between incoming visual information and outgoing motor commands.
expectation: The visual information route will connect to the central nervous system.

effect: The visual route now reaches the brain, forming a seeing control system; it still needs an outgoing connection to the muscles.
reaction: The distinction between seeing the target and producing force is clear.
reason: Motor nerves are the available outgoing route for connecting the control system to muscle commands.
expectation: The motor nerves will connect the seeing control system to the outgoing muscle commands.

effect: The motor nerves now extend from the control system, but their muscle endings remain unattached.
reaction: The unattached endings make the next connection clear.
reason: Connecting the outgoing nerves to the arm should allow muscle commands to reach its muscles.
expectation: The motor nerve endings will connect to the arm muscles.

effect: The control system and arm formed a guided arm, completing the sight-to-command connection and revealing the need for position feedback.
reaction: The incoming and outgoing arrows make the connection easy to follow.
reason: The stretch receptors are described as sensors among muscle fibers with a returning nerve, so they fit the new goal.
expectation: The receptors and sensory nerves will connect the arm's position information back to the control system.

effect: The stretch receptors completed the position-feedback route, showing that the arm can receive position information even with the eyes closed.
reaction: The closed-eyes example made the purpose of the returning signals easy to relate to.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding the stretch receptors was most worthwhile because the result connected muscle sensors to a familiar experience: knowing where an arm is without watching it.

leastWorthwhile.text: Connecting the visual route to the central nervous system felt comparatively predictable, though it was a clear step toward the goal.

surprise.text: The segmented wrapping showed that supporting cells are part of nerves and help signals travel quickly; I had focused on the neuron fibers themselves.

arbitrary.text: None of the actions felt particularly arbitrary; the item descriptions and goals gave each connection a clear purpose.

continue.text: I would continue for another chapter to see how the guided arm works with other body systems. The position-feedback result made me curious, though several connections were predictable.
